definition: The rules for powers of a non-zero base $a$ with integer exponents: $a^{m} \times a^{n} = a^{m+n}$ and $a^{m} \div a^{n} = a^{m-n}$ (both need the same base), $(a^{m})^{n} = a^{mn}$, $a^{0} = 1$ and $a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^{n}}$.
For $a > 0$, $a \neq 1$ and $b > 0$, $\log_{a} b$ is the exponent $x$ for which $a^{x} = b$, so $\log_{10} 1000 = 3$ because $10^{3} = 1000$.
The logarithm with base $\mathrm{e}$, written $\ln x = \log_{\mathrm{e}} x$ and defined only for $x > 0$, so $\ln b = x$ means $\mathrm{e}^{x} = b$.
The irrational constant $\mathrm{e} = 2.71828\ldots$, used as the base of exponential growth and decay models and of the natural logarithm.
